main_body: A wooden choir stall: a tall panelled back with five arched recesses, a canopy/cornice on top, and a front bench with red cushion pads, all drawn straight from the front.
top_band: none that reads as a horizontal surface. Rows 8-11 are a cornice face (brown with gold studs) and row 12 is a light line. The bench seat at rows 37-39 is only a 1-3 row strip, red cushions at row 37-38, with no top surface visible.
evidence: The seat is a seat-kind piece, but its surface is only a 1-2 row strip (red cushion rows 37-38 and a tan edge at row 40) in front of a tall back panel. There is no seat plane seen from above. The cushions read as a thin band, like the guide's 'thin seat' failure. The back is five arched panels painted flat, a vertical face seen head-on. The cornice at the top is a vertical band with a 1-row highlight at row 12, not a top surface. Nothing in the drawing is a horizontal surface seen from above, so the whole drawing is a front elevation.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 11 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile, against 17 and 20 per tile and 38-40 colours in the references, so it is much lower in density. The brown ramp has about 4 steps (very dark, dark, mid, light), and the arched panels are large flat dark fills with little grain. The outline is a tinted dark brown (0% neutral), which is in line with Beodeul. The red cushions are flat bands with no per-pad shading. Next to the cheese stall and the roofed well, it looks thinner and flatter.
